This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The shedding order is held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in an order the site operator has chosen, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, the welded contactor being a condition that cannot be cleared from the edge controller 106 and that requires attention at the equipment.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired. The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that the connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding, and so that controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted from the management service, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its management service will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The sequence is uploaded to the management service when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored and the fault indicator 116 is operated. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time. The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106.

The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling, and the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order.

Seven empty rectangles and one empty diamond are arranged in a single vertical column down the centre of the drawing area, spaced evenly from top to bottom in the following order:

1. a rectangle, the available current determination step, at the top of the column;
2. a rectangle, the sustaining and deficit assignment step;
3. a rectangle, the pilot command step;
4. a rectangle, the connector verification step;
5. a diamond, the staged reduction step, in which the measured branch current is compared with the branch current limit;
6. a rectangle, the ordered shedding step;
7. a rectangle, the welded-contactor isolation step;
8. a rectangle, the conditional reclosure step, at the bottom of the column.

A straight vertical solid line with an arrowhead at its lower end joins each shape in the column to the next shape below it, the arrowhead touching the upper edge of the lower shape. The line into the diamond meets the upper vertex of the diamond, and the line leaving the diamond leaves its lower vertex.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command, such as lighting, ventilation or refrigeration equipment.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides galvanic isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor of the installation, shown as an unnumbered line entering the drawing area, and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained, below which the session is not worth sustaining and the vehicle is liable to terminate it. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations from a management service. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. The edge controller 106 is coupled to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. In one implementation it is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors as that part of the measured branch current which is not accounted for by the sum of the measured connector currents. In another implementation a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load 118 reports it. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin, held in the nonvolatile memory 112, that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution. The share given to a connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that connector channel, and any part of the remainder that cannot be placed for that reason is offered to the other active connector channels.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel. A connector channel whose measured connector current is at or below its assigned current limit has complied. A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel, that is, a further current limit lower than the limit previously assigned to it, and repeats the verification. This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The shedding order is held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in an order the site operator has chosen, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, the welded contactor being a condition that cannot be cleared from the edge controller 106 and that requires attention at the equipment.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired. The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that the connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding, and so that controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted from the management service, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its management service will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The sequence is uploaded to the management service when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored and the fault indicator 116 is operated. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded, and cause the edge controller 106 to perform the allocation, verification, staged reduction and ordered shedding described above when they are executed by the processing unit 132. The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time. The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106.

The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling, and the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, the welded contactor being a condition that cannot be cleared from the edge controller 106 and that requires attention at the equipment.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired. The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that the connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding, and so that controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted from the management service, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its management service will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The sequence is uploaded to the management service when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored and the fault indicator 116 is operated. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded, and cause the edge controller 106 to perform the allocation, verification, staged reduction and ordered shedding described above when they are executed by the processing unit 132. The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time. The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106.

The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling, and the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

lines: FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained, below which the session is not worth sustaining and the vehicle is liable to terminate it. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel.

# FIG. 1

## View
A flat schematic system diagram in plain black line work on a white background, no shading and no text inside the drawing area. All line work sits well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges and filing margins.

## Structures and relationships
A dashed rectangle encloses the whole diagram and represents the charging installation, shown schematically.

Inside it, one horizontal solid line runs across the upper part of the drawing area and represents the branch conductor. Its left end reaches the left side of the dashed rectangle and stops there, indicating the incoming supply.

A small square outline straddles the horizontal line in its left portion and represents the branch current sensor. The horizontal line passes through the square outline and continues to the right of it. The square outline is shown schematically.

Three empty rectangular blocks stand in a row across the lower part of the drawing area, spaced apart. The leftmost block is a first connector channel, the middle block is a second connector channel, and the rightmost block is a non-charging load.

A short vertical line drops from the horizontal line to the top edge of each of the three blocks, connecting all three in parallel to the horizontal line. All three drops lie to the right of the square outline.

A further empty rectangular block sits in the lower left region, below and to the left of the leftmost block, and represents an edge controller.

A solid line leaves the right side of the edge controller block and runs horizontally beneath the row of three blocks, representing an isolated local bus. One short vertical branch rises from this bus line to the bottom edge of the leftmost block and another rises to the bottom edge of the middle block. The bus line does not touch the rightmost block.

A dashed line runs from the square outline down and to the left to the top edge of the edge controller block, representing the sensing connection to the edge controller. It touches none of the three blocks.

## Numerals appearing on this sheet
- 100 charging installation: leader ends on the dashed enclosing rectangle.
- 102 branch conductor: leader ends on the horizontal line, right of the square outline and clear of the vertical drops.
- 104 branch current sensor: leader ends on the square outline.
- 106 edge controller: leader ends well inside the lower left block.
- 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the horizontal bus line between the edge controller block and the first branch rising from it.
- 118 non-charging load: leader ends well inside the rightmost block of the row.
- 120 first connector channel: leader ends well inside the leftmost block of the row.
- 140 second connector channel: leader ends well inside the middle block of the row.

Part names above are semantic identifiers only. They do not appear as drawing text.

Seven empty rectangles and one empty diamond stand in a single vertical column down the centre of the drawing area, evenly spaced from top to bottom in this order:

1. rectangle, the available current determination step, at the top;
2. rectangle, the sustaining and deficit assignment step;
3. rectangle, the pilot command step;
4. rectangle, the connector verification step;
5. diamond, the staged reduction step, at which the measured branch current is compared with the branch current limit;
6. rectangle, the ordered shedding step;
7. rectangle, the welded-contactor isolation step;
8. rectangle, the conditional reclosure step, at the bottom.

A straight vertical solid line with an arrowhead at its lower end joins each shape to the shape below it, the arrowhead touching the upper edge of the lower shape. The line into the diamond meets its upper vertex and the line out of the diamond leaves its lower vertex.

A solid line leaves the left vertex of the diamond, runs left to a vertical return path at the left of the column, rises to the height of the topmost rectangle, then runs right and ends with an arrowhead touching the left edge of the topmost rectangle.

A second solid line leaves the right edge of the bottom rectangle, runs right to a vertical return path at the right of the column, rises to the height of the topmost rectangle, then runs left and ends with an arrowhead touching the right edge of the topmost rectangle.

Neither return path crosses the column or the other return path.

A flat schematic diagram of one connector channel in plain black line work on white, no shading and no text inside the drawing area. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

Below the contactor the line resumes, turns right and runs horizontally to the right side of the dashed rectangle. A closed ring outline encircles this horizontal run without touching it and represents the connector current sensor.

An empty rectangular block sits in the lower region of the dashed rectangle, below the horizontal run, and represents the control-pilot interface.

Where the horizontal run reaches the right side of the dashed rectangle it meets an empty rectangular block straddling that side, representing the vehicle connector. A short open-ended notch is cut into the right face of this block, shown schematically as the mating face.

To the right of the dashed rectangle a larger rounded rectangle represents an electric vehicle, shown schematically. A short solid line runs from the notch to the left side of the rounded rectangle. A second solid line runs from the right side of the control-pilot interface block, up and to the right, crosses the dashed rectangle and joins the left side of the rounded rectangle, representing the control pilot signalling path.

A solid horizontal line enters from the left, crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region and represents the isolated local bus. Inside the dashed rectangle it branches to the left side of the control-pilot interface block, upward to the hinged bar, and to the ring outline.

content.content:
1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command, such as lighting, ventilation or refrigeration equipment.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides galvanic isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained, below which the session is not worth sustaining and the vehicle is liable to terminate it. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations from a management service. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18	
19	At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. In one implementation it is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors as that part of the measured branch current which is not accounted for by the sum of the measured connector currents. In another implementation a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load 118 reports it. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin, held in the nonvolatile memory 112, that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution. The share given to a connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that connector channel, and any part of the remainder that cannot be placed for that reason is offered to the other active connector channels.
22	
23	At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.
24	
25	At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel. A connector channel whose measured connector current is at or below its assigned current limit has complied. A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel, that is, a further current limit lower than the limit previously assigned to it, and repeats the verification. This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.
26	
27	At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.
28	
29	At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The shedding order is held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in an order the site operator has chosen, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
30	
31	The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.
32	
33	At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, the welded contactor being a condition that cannot be cleared from the edge controller 106 and that requires attention at the equipment.
34	
35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired. The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that the connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding, and so that controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.
36	
37	The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted from the management service, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.
38	
39	During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its management service will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.
40	
41	Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The sequence is uploaded to the management service when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.
42	
43	The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored and the fault indicator 116 is operated. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.
44	
45	The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded, and cause the edge controller 106 to perform the allocation, verification, staged reduction and ordered shedding described above when they are executed by the processing unit 132. The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time. The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106.
46	
47	The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102.
48	
49	The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling, and the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order.
50	
51	The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command, such as lighting, ventilation or refrigeration equipment.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides galvanic isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained, below which the session is not worth sustaining and the vehicle is liable to terminate it. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations from a management service. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. In one implementation it is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors as that part of the measured branch current which is not accounted for by the sum of the measured connector currents. In another implementation a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load 118 reports it. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin, held in the nonvolatile memory 112, that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. The share given to a connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that connector channel, and any part of the remainder that cannot be placed for that reason is offered to the other active connector channels.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together.
