1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:

a plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the respective one of the vehicle connectors, and a control-pilot interface, each connector channel being associated with a local connector identifier;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels; and

a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor, the controller being configured to:

store, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;

at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtract a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assign the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;

send the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;

send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and

responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, open the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of the identified active connector channel.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

5. The apparatus of claim 4, wherein the controller is further configured to draw the randomized recovery delay within a stored range separately for each connector channel that has been opened.

6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate a local fault indicator.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.

8. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

9. The apparatus of claim 8, wherein the share of the remainder distributed to an active connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that active connector channel, and the controller is configured to offer to the other active connector channels a part of the remainder that is not distributed by reason of that limit.

10. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing galvanic isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.

11. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to the opening of the contactors in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.

12. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the controller is configured, during the outage of the network interface, not to start a charging session at a newly connected one of the vehicle connectors unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of the connector channel of that newly connected one of the vehicle connectors and the signed local authorization token has not expired.

13. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the controller is configured to append meter records of the charging sessions to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory, each appended meter record carrying a value computed over that meter record together with a preceding state of the tamper-evident local sequence, and to upload the tamper-evident local sequence through the network interface when communication returns.

14. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a service input, wherein the controller is configured, on entry of a commissioning mode through the service input, to associate the local connector identifiers with the contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded connector channel and determining which connector current sensor responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition.

input.summary: Wrote the complete first draft of the application from the inventor's disclosure: title, cross-reference and government-support sections (both "Not applicable."), field, background, summary, brief description of the drawings, detailed description keyed to four figures, 23 claims in three statutory classes, abstract, a 27-entry reference-numeral table, and four self-contained figure briefs (system diagram, connector-channel detail, controller block diagram, process flow). Important caveat on prior art: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references at all and the directory contains only that empty index, so no citation was possible and no art was available to write around. The art you were given is therefore incomplete, and claim scope was set only against the disclosure and general background knowledge of branch-shared EV charging; a real search may require narrowing claim 1.
reasoning: Claim 1 recites the disclosed essential relationship and nothing more: per-connector sensing plus an independent upstream branch measurement, allocation from a branch limit reduced by measured non-charging load and a configurable safety reserve, minimum-sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot command with per-connector verification, and then the two-stage protective response of a reduced pilot command followed, only if the measured branch current stays above the limit for a verification interval, by opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order. The inventor identified exactly this combination as essential, so it is the broadest statement the description supports.

Deliberately left out of claim 1: the isolated local bus and its galvanic isolation (moved to claim 10), reclosure conditions (claim 4), welded-contactor isolation (claim 6), the offline token and last accepted branch limit (claims 11 and 12), tamper-evident meter records (claim 13), and the commissioning mapping (claims 14 and 15). Each is described in the disclosure as a supported additional feature rather than part of the essential relationship, so each is scope that claim 1 should not spend.

The dependent ladder is graduated rather than decorative. Claim 2 is the nearest fallback, adding that the connector current sensors identify which channel is out of compliance so the reduced pilot command is aimed at it. Claim 3 adds re-measurement after each contactor opening, which is what makes the shedding minimal rather than wholesale. Claims 4 and 5 add the three-part reclosure gate and the per-channel randomized delay. Claim 6 adds welded-contactor detection and branch-wide inhibit. Claims 7, 8 and 9 pin down the allocation policy. Claims 11 to 13 cover offline operation and accounting, and claims 14 and 15 cover installation mapping, each of which is separately arguable.

Three statutory classes are claimed because different parties infringe them: the apparatus (claim 1) is made by the equipment manufacturer, the method (claim 17) is performed by the site operator running the controller, and the non-transitory medium (claim 23) is distributed by whoever supplies the firmware. Claim 23 required a supporting sentence in the detailed description about instructions carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, which is the only place the description was widened for claim support.

Two facts the disclosure states but does not explain had to be made enabling without inventing anything. The measured non-charging branch load is described as obtainable either as the part of the measured branch current not accounted for by the sum of the connector currents, or from a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load, and only the second-hand generic phrase "measured non-charging branch load" appears in claim 1; the derivation is confined to dependent claim 16. Distribution "according to energy deficit" is described as giving a larger share to a larger deficit, with proportional distribution named as one implementation, and only the general phrase appears in claim 1.

The specification carries the technical-problem explanations that later prosecution would be built from: why a pilot-signalled limit is only a request that a vehicle may ignore, why an unmeasured auxiliary load defeats a purely computed allocation, why ordered shedding under measurement is preferable to letting the branch overcurrent device trip, why the randomized recovery delay prevents synchronized restoration, and why a consistent but transposed wiring map makes every subsequent verification appear to succeed. These are stated before they are needed rather than left to argument.

Four figures were used. FIG. 1 (system) and FIG. 2 (connector-channel detail) are split rather than combined because a single sheet would have exceeded eight numerals; the second connector channel is drawn as a block and described as of the same construction, so its internal parts need no duplicate numerals. FIG. 3 is the controller block diagram and FIG. 4 is the operational flow, whose eight step numerals cover allocation, verification, staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure. Commissioning mapping is described in text only, since adding a fifth sheet was not needed to identify any part.

Every part whose appearance the disclosure does not fix is specified in the figure briefs as a plain rectangle, ring, or rounded outline and expressly marked as shown schematically, so no drawing convention leaks into the specification or claims.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/ contains only INDEX.md, whose reference table is empty, so there was no document to read, cite, or design around, and the Background contains no citations. In place of a citation-based strategy, claim 1 was built on the feature the disclosure itself identifies as essential and which is the hardest to arrive at from ordinary load-sharing practice: the branch current sensor upstream of every contactor is treated as an independent safety authority, and an overcurrent is answered first by a reduced pilot command, then, only if the measured branch current is still above the limit after a verification interval, by opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order with the branch measurement re-read between openings. That converts an unanswered signalled reduction into a bounded, ordered, measured removal of load, and it is separable from the two things a searcher would most likely find, namely pure pilot-signalled allocation among connectors and a plain overcurrent trip or simultaneous shutdown. Vocabulary was chosen to describe the invention on its own terms, using connector channel, assigned current limit, available charging current, staged reduction, ordered shedding order and conditional reclosure. The dependent ladder gives fallbacks in decreasing breadth so that a later search can be met by retreating to the aimed reduced pilot command, then minimal shedding with re-measurement, then the three-condition reclosure gate with per-channel randomized delay, then welded-contactor branch inhibit, then the offline signed token combination, then the confirm-before-store commissioning mapping. Because no search was run, the attorney should re-test claim 1 against real art before filing.
input.answer:
The draft is written and complete in draft/ and figures/.

**Body text.** Title, cross-reference and government-support ("Not applicable." in both, as the filing notes direct), field, background, summary, brief description of the drawings, detailed description, claims and abstract.

**Claims.** 23 claims in three statutory classes. Claim 1 (apparatus) recites the disclosed essential relationship: connector channels each with a contactor, connector current sensor and control-pilot interface; a branch current sensor upstream of all contactors; and a controller that at each allocation interval subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit, assigns minimum sustaining currents first, distributes the remainder by energy deficit, commands the limits over the control pilot and verifies each connector current, then sends a reduced pilot command on branch overcurrent and, only if the measured branch current stays above the limit for a verification interval, opens contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order. Claim 17 is the corresponding method and claim 23 a non-transitory computer-readable medium. Dependents cover aimed reduced pilot commands, minimal shedding with re-measurement, the three-condition reclosure gate with per-channel randomized delay, welded-contactor isolation and branch inhibit, allocation policy details, the isolated local bus, offline operation on a signed local token and last accepted branch limit, tamper-evident meter records, and confirm-before-store commissioning mapping.

**Drawings.** Four briefs: FIG. 1 system diagram, FIG. 2 connector-channel detail, FIG. 3 controller block diagram, FIG. 4 process flow. Each is self-contained, lists at most eight numerals, and stays within the 2800-character limit. draft/numerals.md holds 27 numerals, each appearing once against one part name, and every numeral used in the text or on a sheet is in the table.

**One thing you should know before relying on this.** prior_art/ contains only an empty INDEX.md with no rows, so there was nothing to cite and nothing to write around. The Background therefore carries no citations, and claim 1 was scoped against your disclosure and general background knowledge only. Treat the available art as incomplete: a real search may well require narrowing claim 1, and the dependent ladder was built with that retreat in mind.

Important caveat on prior art: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references at all and the directory contains only that empty index, so no citation was possible and no art was available to write around. The art you were given is therefore incomplete, and claim scope was set only against the disclosure and general background knowledge of branch-shared EV charging; a real search may require narrowing claim 1.
reasoning: Claim 1 recites the disclosed essential relationship and nothing more: per-connector sensing plus an independent upstream branch measurement, allocation from a branch limit reduced by measured non-charging load and a configurable safety reserve, minimum-sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot command with per-connector verification, and then the two-stage protective response of a reduced pilot command followed, only if the measured branch current stays above the limit for a verification interval, by opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order. The inventor identified exactly this combination as essential, so it is the broadest statement the description supports.

Deliberately left out of claim 1: the isolated local bus and its galvanic isolation (moved to claim 10), reclosure conditions (claim 4), welded-contactor isolation (claim 6), the offline token and last accepted branch limit (claims 11 and 12), tamper-evident meter records (claim 13), and the commissioning mapping (claims 14 and 15). Each is described in the disclosure as a supported additional feature rather than part of the essential relationship, so each is scope that claim 1 should not spend.

The dependent ladder is graduated rather than decorative. Claim 2 is the nearest fallback, adding that the connector current sensors identify which channel is out of compliance so the reduced pilot command is aimed at it. Claim 3 adds re-measurement after each contactor opening, which is what makes the shedding minimal rather than wholesale. Claims 4 and 5 add the three-part reclosure gate and the per-channel randomized delay. Claim 6 adds welded-contactor detection and branch-wide inhibit. Claims 7, 8 and 9 pin down the allocation policy. Claims 11 to 13 cover offline operation and accounting, and claims 14 and 15 cover installation mapping, each of which is separately arguable.

Three statutory classes are claimed because different parties infringe them: the apparatus (claim 1) is made by the equipment manufacturer, the method (claim 17) is performed by the site operator running the controller, and the non-transitory medium (claim 23) is distributed by whoever supplies the firmware. Claim 23 required a supporting sentence in the detailed description about instructions carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, which is the only place the description was widened for claim support.

Two facts the disclosure states but does not explain had to be made enabling without inventing anything. The measured non-charging branch load is described as obtainable either as the part of the measured branch current not accounted for by the sum of the connector currents, or from a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load, and only the second-hand generic phrase "measured non-charging branch load" appears in claim 1; the derivation is confined to dependent claim 16. Distribution "according to energy deficit" is described as giving a larger share to a larger deficit, with proportional distribution named as one implementation, and only the general phrase appears in claim 1.

The specification carries the technical-problem explanations that later prosecution would be built from: why a pilot-signalled limit is only a request that a vehicle may ignore, why an unmeasured auxiliary load defeats a purely computed allocation, why ordered shedding under measurement is preferable to letting the branch overcurrent device trip, why the randomized recovery delay prevents synchronized restoration, and why a consistent but transposed wiring map makes every subsequent verification appear to succeed. These are stated before they are needed rather than left to argument.

Four figures were used. FIG. 1 (system) and FIG. 2 (connector-channel detail) are split rather than combined because a single sheet would have exceeded eight numerals; the second connector channel is drawn as a block and described as of the same construction, so its internal parts need no duplicate numerals. FIG. 3 is the controller block diagram and FIG. 4 is the operational flow, whose eight step numerals cover allocation, verification, staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure. Commissioning mapping is described in text only, since adding a fifth sheet was not needed to identify any part.

Every part whose appearance the disclosure does not fix is specified in the figure briefs as a plain rectangle, ring, or rounded outline and expressly marked as shown schematically, so no drawing convention leaks into the specification or claims.

input.content: A controller allocates one electrical branch among electric vehicle connectors whose combined ratings exceed the branch current limit. Each connector channel has a contactor, a connector current sensor and a control-pilot interface, and a branch current sensor measures branch current upstream of the contactors. At each allocation interval the controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assigns a minimum sustaining current to each active connector channel that can receive it, distributes the remainder according to stored energy-deficit values, sends the resulting assigned current limits through the control-pilot interfaces, and verifies each connector current with the corresponding connector current sensor. When measured branch current remains above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command, the controller opens the contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

A derivation that is merely obvious from the disclosed sensors is not source support.
80	  - Suggested fix: Cancel claim 16 and delete the two implementation sentences from ¶19, leaving the disclosed statement that the edge controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit.
81	- **[critical] Component-technology and enclosure variants presented as embodiments have no source** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶45 (last sentence) and ¶47) - None of these variants appears in the disclosure or the conversation. The disclosure names only "a controllable contactor", "a connector current sensor", "a branch current sensor" and "an isolated local bus", and says nothing about sensor technology, solid-state switching, bus media, or how the channels and controller are housed. Each is a variant presented as part of the invention and must trace to a source; conventionality and plausibility are not support.
82	  - Suggested fix: Delete the last sentence of ¶45 and the whole of ¶47. The disclosed parts remain described at ¶¶5, 7 and 9 in the inventor's own terms.
83	- **[critical] DC charging and multi-outlet connector embodiments are added to the invention** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶49) - The disclosure describes control-pilot current limits sent to vehicles at EV connectors and says nothing about direct current charging, about a control-pilot interface signalling an available current to vehicle-side equipment, or about a connector having more than one physical outlet and being treated as a single channel for allocation and shedding. These are added embodiments and an added allocation/shedding rule.
84	  - Suggested fix: Delete ¶49 apart from its opening clause, retaining only "The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling."
85	- **[major] "Galvanic isolation" is a specific characterisation the disclosure does not give the isolated local bus** (draft/09-claims.md claim 10; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶7) - The sources say only that the controller communicates over "an isolated local bus". I am flagging this as major rather than critical because "isolated" is the disclosed word and the candidate has narrowed rather than broadened it, but the specific term is still untraced.

# Previous review - verdict: fail

The draft is a well-organised, internally coherent application whose backbone - branch-limited allocation, per-connector verification, staged reduction, ordered contactor shedding, conditional reclosure, welded-contactor isolation, offline authorization, tamper-evident records and commissioning mapping - traces cleanly to input/disclosure.md (which is identical to the single USER message in input/conversation.md). Numerals are used consistently: every numeral in numerals.md labels exactly one part, and each part carries the same numeral everywhere in draft/08-detailed-description.md and in the figure briefs. The Brief Description of the Drawings matches what the four briefs describe, and no numeral is defined twice or reused.

Two mechanical limits on this review: (1) figures/ contains only the four Markdown briefs - there are no rendered-*.png files, and review/figure-audit-evidence.json does not exist in this workspace, so I could not verify pixels, printed numerals, leaders or geometry; the "each described figure has a drawing sheet" and "27 numerals absent from every drawing" mechanical failures are the same fact, and I have not re-reported them as findings. My figure comments are therefore brief-versus-text only. (2) prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references ("| (none) | | |") and the draft contains no [REF:...] citation anywhere, so there is nothing to check under citation honesty; the background makes only uncited general-field statements. The abstract is now 146 words, so the previous QA failure (193 words) is cleared.

The substantive problem is disclosure fidelity. The description and claims add a layer of implementation specifics the inventor never supplied: a hash-chain construction for the meter sequence (claim 13), a stored range and per-channel draw for the recovery delay (claim 5), a requested-current cap with re-offer of the residue (claim 9), a fault indicator on a commissioning mismatch (claim 15), two named ways of obtaining the non-charging branch load including a dedicated sensor (claim 16), and a set of component-technology and DC-charging variants. Nine of these are recited in claims, which under the instructions makes them critical. Lower-severity items are added definitions and attributions that are plausible but untraced.

## Mechanical checks that did not pass

- **Every specification numeral appears in a drawing** (fail): 27 reference numeral(s) are used in the specification but absent from every drawing. Add each missing numeral to an appropriate focused sheet or redistribute the existing drawing plan. Do not remove a disclosed part, numeral definition, or supporting text to silence this check.

## Reviewer findings

- **[critical] Hash-chain construction of the tamper-evident meter sequence is not in the disclosure, and is claimed** (draft/09-claims.md claim 13; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶41; draft/06-summary.md ¶9) - The disclosure says only that meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded later. It says nothing about how tamper-evidence is achieved. The candidate supplies a specific chained-value construction and then claims it, so the only support for claim 13 is the candidate's own added text.
  - Suggested fix: Delete the chained-value limitation from claim 13 so that it recites only appending meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory and uploading it when communication returns, and delete the sentence "Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined." from ¶41.
- **[critical] Stored range, per-channel draw and neighbouring-branch coordination added to the randomized recovery delay, and claimed** (draft/09-claims.md claim 5; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶35; draft/06-summary.md ¶7) - The disclosure recites the randomized recovery delay as one of three reclosure preconditions and gives it no parameters. The candidate adds that the delay is drawn within a stored range, drawn separately per connector channel, and coordinates recovery with controllers at other branches - a system context (neighbouring branches with their own controllers) that appears nowhere in the sources. Claim 5 recites the stored range and the per-channel draw.
  - Suggested fix: Cancel claim 5. In ¶35 replace the added sentence with the disclosed condition alone ("A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding.") and delete ", and controllers at neighbouring branches," from summary ¶7.
- **[critical] Requested-current cap on the deficit share, and re-offer of the undistributable residue, are not disclosed and are claimed** (draft/09-claims.md claim 9; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶21) - The disclosure stores a requested current per active connector but says only that the remaining current is distributed according to energy deficit. It never states that the share is capped at the requested current, nor that a capped residue is redistributed. Claim 9 recites both rules; its only support is the candidate's own paragraph.
  - Suggested fix: Cancel claim 9 and delete the final sentence of ¶21 ("The share given to a connector channel is limited ... offered to the other active connector channels."); the disclosed distribution rule already supported by claim 8 and by the preceding sentences of ¶21 is retained.
- **[critical] Fault-indicator response to a commissioning mismatch is not disclosed and is claimed** (draft/09-claims.md claim 15; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶43) - The disclosure's commissioning process ends at the storage condition: the association is stored only if the sensed channel agrees. It attaches the local fault indicator solely to the welded-contactor condition. The candidate extends the fault indicator to a wiring mismatch and to a no-response case and claims that extension.
  - Suggested fix: Delete the "and to operate a local fault indicator ..." clause from claim 15, leaving the disclosed storage condition, and in ¶43 replace the sentence with "Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored."
- **[critical] Two named ways of obtaining the non-charging branch load, including a dedicated sensor, are added; one is claimed** (draft/09-claims.md claim 16; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶19) - The disclosure says the controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load; it never says how that quantity is measured. - **[critical] Component-technology and enclosure variants presented as embodiments have no source** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶45 (last sentence) and ¶47) - None of these variants appears in the disclosure or the conversation. - **[critical] DC charging and multi-outlet connector embodiments are added to the invention** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶49) - The disclosure describes control-pilot current limits sent to vehicles at EV connectors and says nothing about direct current charging, about a control-pilot interface signalling an available current to vehicle-side equipment, or about a connector having more than one physical outlet and being treated as a single channel for allocation and shedding.   - Suggested fix: Delete ¶49 apart from its opening clause, retaining only "The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling."
- **[major] "Galvanic isolation" is a specific characterisation the disclosure does not give the isolated local bus** (draft/09-claims.md claim 10; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶7) - The sources say only that the controller communicates over "an isolated local bus". The candidate specifies the kind of isolation and recites it as a claim limitation, so claim 10's characterising feature rests on candidate-introduced text rather than on the disclosure. I am flagging this as major rather than critical because "isolated" is the disclosed word and the candidate has narrowed rather than broadened it, but the specific term is still untraced.
  - Suggested fix: Replace "galvanic isolation" with "isolation" in claim 10 and in ¶7, so both read in the disclosed terms ("the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels").
- **[major] Derivation of the stored requested current is added** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶13) - The disclosure lists the requested current among the stored per-session values and never says where the value comes from. The candidate asserts two specific sources for it (the channel rating and demand reported over the control pilot). Nothing in the sources says the control-pilot interface reports a demand.

- **[major] Token issuer and signature verification against a stored key are added** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶37) - The disclosure says the controller stores a signed local authorization token that authorizes a connector and has an expiry. It does not say the management service issues it, and it does not disclose a stored verification key inside the controller - that is an added element of the apparatus. The connector-authorizing and expiry attributes are supported; the issuer and the stored key are not.

1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:

a plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the respective one of the vehicle connectors, and a control-pilot interface, each connector channel being associated with a local connector identifier;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels; and

a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor, the controller being configured to:

store, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;

at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtract a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assign the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;

send the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;

send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and

responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, open the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of the identified active connector channel.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate a local fault indicator.

6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

8. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.

9. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.

10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the controller is configured, during the outage of the network interface, not to start a charging session at a newly connected one of the vehicle connectors unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of the connector channel of that newly connected one of the vehicle connectors and the signed local authorization token has not expired.

11. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the controller is configured to append meter records of the charging sessions to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory, and to upload the tamper-evident local sequence through the network interface when communication returns.

12. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a service input, wherein the controller is configured, on entry of a commissioning mode through the service input, to associate the local connector identifiers with the contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded connector channel and determining which connector current sensor responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition.

13. The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the controller is configured to store an association between the local connector identifier of the commanded connector channel and the contactor of the commanded connector channel only after the responding connector current sensor is the connector current sensor of the commanded connector channel.

14. A method of controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of connector channels supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of vehicle connectors of the plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor and a control-pilot interface, the method comprising:

storing, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;

measuring a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels with a branch current sensor;

at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtracting a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assigning the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distributing a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;

sending the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verifying a connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;

sending a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and

responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:

a plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the respective one of the vehicle connectors, and a control-pilot interface, each connector channel being associated with a local connector identifier;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels; and

a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor, the controller being configured to:

store, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;

at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtract a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assign the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;

send the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;

send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and

responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, open the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of the identified active connector channel.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate a local fault indicator.

6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

8. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.

9. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.

10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the controller is configured, during the outage of the network interface, not to start a charging session at a newly connected one of the vehicle connectors unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of the connector channel of that newly connected one of the vehicle connectors and the signed local authorization token has not expired.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command, such as lighting, ventilation or refrigeration equipment.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides galvanic isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained, below which the session is not worth sustaining and the vehicle is liable to terminate it. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations from a management service. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. In one implementation it is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors as that part of the measured branch current which is not accounted for by the sum of the measured connector currents. In another implementation a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load 118 reports it. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin, held in the nonvolatile memory 112, that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution. The share given to a connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that connector channel, and any part of the remainder that cannot be placed for that reason is offered to the other active connector channels.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel. A connector channel whose measured connector current is at or below its assigned current limit has complied. A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel, that is, a further current limit lower than the limit previously assigned to it, and repeats the verification. This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The shedding order is held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in an order the site operator has chosen, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, the welded contactor being a condition that cannot be cleared from the edge controller 106 and that requires attention at the equipment.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired. The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that the connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding, and so that controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted from the management service, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its management service will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The sequence is uploaded to the management service when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored and the fault indicator 116 is operated. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded, and cause the edge controller 106 to perform the allocation, verification, staged reduction and ordered shedding described above when they are executed by the processing unit 132. The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time. The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106.

The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling, and the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired. The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that the connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding, and so that controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two.
