1:1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:
19:2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of the identified active connector channel.
21:3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
23:4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.
25:5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate a local fault indicator.
27:6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.
29:7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.
31:8. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.
33:9. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.
35:10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the controller is configured, during the outage of the network interface, not to start a charging session at a newly connected one of the vehicle connectors unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of the connector channel of that newly connected one of the vehicle connectors and the signed local authorization token has not expired.
37:11. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the controller is configured to append meter records of the charging sessions to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory, and to upload the tamper-evident local sequence through the network interface when communication returns.
39:12. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a service input, wherein the controller is configured, on entry of a commissioning mode through the service input, to associate the local connector identifiers with the contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded connector channel and determining which connector current sensor responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition.
41:13. The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the controller is configured to store an association between the local connector identifier of the commanded connector channel and the contactor of the commanded connector channel only after the responding connector current sensor is the connector current sensor of the commanded connector channel.
43:14. A method of controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of connector channels supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of vehicle connectors of the plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor and a control-pilot interface, the method comprising:
57:15. The method of claim 14, further comprising measuring the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and opening no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
59:16. The method of claim 14, further comprising withholding reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.
61:17. The method of claim 14, further comprising recording a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, inhibiting the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and operating a local fault indicator.
63:18. The method of claim 14, further comprising holding a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in a nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of a network interface through which remote schedules and remote authorizations are received, continuing charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order, and not starting a charging session at a newly connected one of the vehicle connectors unless the signed local authorization token authorizes a local connector identifier of the connector channel of that newly connected one of the vehicle connectors and the signed local authorization token has not expired.
65:19. The method of claim 14, further comprising, on entry of a commissioning mode through a service input, associating local connector identifiers with the contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded connector channel, determining which connector current sensor responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition, and storing an association between the local connector identifier of the commanded connector channel and the contactor of the commanded connector channel only after the responding connector current sensor is the connector current sensor of the commanded connector channel.

content.text: All findings are addressed and the files are consistent.

input.summary: Removed every candidate-supplied implementation detail the review identified as untraced, cancelled the four claims that rested on it, renumbered the claim set from 23 to 19 claims with corrected dependencies, fixed both antecedent-basis warnings, added the description sentence that grounds the claim 2 linkage, and corrected the FIG. 4 flow so welded-contactor isolation no longer runs unconditionally into conditional reclosure. The reference-numeral table is unchanged and still exact: all 27 numerals remain in use in the description and every one of them is listed on a figure sheet.
reasoning: The seven critical findings were resolved by deletion rather than by rewriting around them, because each rested on text the draft itself had introduced. The chained-value construction, the recovery-delay parameters and neighbouring-branch context, the requested-current cap with residue re-offer, the fault indicator on a commissioning mismatch, the two named ways of obtaining the non-charging branch load, the component-technology and enclosure variants, and the DC and multi-outlet embodiments are all gone from the description, the summary and the claims.

Four claims were cancelled: the recovery-delay parameters, the requested-current cap, the non-charging-load derivation, and the computer-readable-medium claim. The claim set was renumbered 1 to 19 and every dependency re-pointed, so the offline-authorization pair now depends on claim 9 and the commissioning storage condition on claim 12. Two statutory classes remain, apparatus and method, and both now recite only disclosed controller operations.

Cancelling the medium claim cost a statutory class, which the filing notes asked for. That was the right trade: the disclosure never mentions instructions, a program or a medium, and a class supported only by candidate-written description text is worse than no class at all. The method claims are unaffected because they recite operations the inventor described.

Claim 1 is untouched. Every deletion was of a dependent-claim limitation or of description text that no surviving claim needs, so the broadest claim and the essential relationship it recites, closed-loop allocation with independent upstream branch sensing followed by staged reduction and ordered shedding, are exactly as before.

The two antecedent warnings were genuine and were fixed by rewording rather than by adding recitations: claim 9 now says "subject to opening the contactors ... in the stored shedding order", which draws on the antecedent already established in claim 1, and claim 13 recites "an association" on first use. The "claim word not in description" warning lists only the word "claim" itself, which is inherent to dependent-claim form and cannot be removed without breaking the claims.

For the loose claim 2 linkage I widened the description rather than narrowing the claim, adding to the staged reduction step that the reduced pilot command is directed to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step as drawing more than its assigned limit. Both behaviours were already described; the sentence now states the combination claim 2 recites.

The FIG. 4 correction follows the disclosed inhibit, not the drawing. Because a recorded welded-contactor condition inhibits the other contactors, those contactors are not reclosed while it stands, so the brief now marks the line into conditional reclosure as the no-welded-condition path and terminates the flow at welded-contactor isolation. The description was synchronized in both directions: the welded step states that inhibited contactors are not reclosed, and the reclosure step states the condition under which it is reached. No numeral was added, since a terminator is flow annotation.

Beyond the listed findings I removed three further untraced attributions of the same kind, so the same objection does not recur: the management service as the party that issues the token, sets the last accepted branch limit and receives the meter upload, now stated as passing through the network interface; the rationale that a vehicle terminates below the minimum sustaining current; and the assertion that a welded condition cannot be cleared from the controller.

No disclosed part, numeral or figure was deleted to satisfy any check. All 27 numerals are still used in the description and still appear on exactly one focused sheet each, the four figure briefs remain within the character limit, and the brief description of the drawings still matches what the briefs depict.
changes: draft/09-claims.md: cancelled the recovery-delay-parameters claim, the requested-current-cap claim, the non-charging-load-derivation claim and the computer-readable-medium claim; renumbered the remaining claims 1 to 19 and re-pointed all dependencies; deleted the chained-value limitation from the tamper-evident claim; deleted the fault-indicator clause from the commissioning-storage claim; changed "galvanic isolation" to "isolation" in the isolated-local-bus claim; reworded "subject to the opening of the contactors" and "the association" to cure antecedent basis in claims 9, 13, 18 and 19.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: deleted the named examples of the non-charging load; changed "galvanic isolation" to "isolation"; deleted the derivation of the requested current and shortened the energy-deficit and minimum-sustaining-current definitions; deleted the two non-charging-load implementation sentences and the placement of the safety reserve in nonvolatile memory; deleted the requested-current cap and residue re-offer; added the clause directing the reduced pilot command to the channel identified at the connector verification step; replaced the nonvolatile placement and site-operator attribution of the shedding order with the stored shedding order; shortened the leakage-threshold definition; replaced the recovery-delay parameter sentence with the disclosed condition; deleted the token issuer and stored-key clauses; deleted the hash-chain sentence; deleted the fault indicator on a commissioning mismatch; deleted the programmed-processor, computer-readable-medium, sensor-technology, bus-media, contactor-type and enclosure variants and the DC and multi-outlet embodiments; replaced management-service attributions with the network interface; added that inhibited contactors are not reclosed while a welded-contactor condition stands and that conditional reclosure is reached where no such condition has been recorded.
draft/06-summary.md: removed the neighbouring-branch coordination from the recovery-delay aspect and replaced the closing sentence with "Corresponding methods are also disclosed."

figures/fig-04.md: stated that the line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step is the no-welded-condition path, added the short line and small solid square terminator showing that the flow ends at welded-contactor isolation where the condition has been recorded, routed the right return path outboard of and clear of that terminator, and condensed the brief to stay within the character limit.
input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged in substance, and no limitation was added in this revision. prior_art/INDEX.md still lists no references, so there is nothing to cite and no art to design around; the Background continues to make uncited general-field statements only. Claim 1 still rests on the disclosed essential relationship: the branch current sensor upstream of every contactor acts as an independent safety authority, an overcurrent is answered first by a reduced pilot command, and only if the measured branch current remains above the limit for a verification interval are contactors opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. The fallback ladder is shorter after four cancellations but still graduated: aimed reduced pilot command, minimal shedding with re-measurement, the three-condition reclosure gate, welded-contactor branch inhibit, the withheld minimum sustaining current, larger-deficit-larger-share distribution, the isolated local bus, offline operation on a signed local token and last accepted branch limit, tamper-evident meter records, and confirm-before-store commissioning mapping. Because no search was run, claim 1 should be re-tested against real art before filing.
input.answer:
Every listed item is fixed.

**Disclosure fidelity (7 critical, 4 major, 6 minor).** All candidate-supplied implementation detail is out of the application: the chained-value construction for the meter sequence, the recovery-delay range and per-channel draw with its neighbouring-branch context, the requested-current cap and residue re-offer, the fault indicator on a commissioning mismatch, both named ways of obtaining the non-charging branch load, the component-technology, bus-media and enclosure variants, the DC and multi-outlet embodiments, "galvanic" isolation, the derivation of the requested current, the token issuer and stored verification key, the programmed-processor and medium implementation, the energy-deficit baseline and update mechanism, the bounded leakage-threshold definition, the placement of the safety reserve and shedding order in memory 112, the examples of non-charging load, and the site-operator attribution of the shedding order. I also removed three untraced attributions of the same kind that were not on the list, so the objection does not recur: the management service as token issuer, limit source and upload target; the rationale for the minimum sustaining current; and the claim that a welded condition cannot be cleared from the controller.

**Claims.** Four claims are cancelled (recovery-delay parameters, requested-current cap, non-charging-load derivation, and the computer-readable medium). The set is renumbered 1 to 19 with all dependencies re-pointed. Cancelling the medium claim drops one statutory class the filing notes asked for; the disclosure does not mention instructions, a program or a medium, so that class had no source support. Apparatus and method claims remain, and claim 1 is unchanged.

**Antecedent warnings.** Claim 9 now reads "subject to opening the contactors ... in the stored shedding order", using the antecedent set in claim 1, and claim 13 recites "an association" on first use. Claims 18 and 19 got the same treatment. The remaining warning lists only the word "claim", which is inherent to dependent-claim form.

**Claim 2 linkage.** The staged reduction paragraph now states that the reduced pilot command is directed to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step as drawing more than its assigned limit, so the description states the combination claim 2 recites.

**FIG. 4.** The brief now marks the line into conditional reclosure as the path taken where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded, and shows the flow ending at welded-contactor isolation with a short line to a small solid square terminator, with the right return path routed clear of it. This follows the disclosed inhibit, and the description was synchronized at both steps. No numeral was added, since a terminator is flow annotation.

**Numerals and sheets.** Nothing was deleted to silence the two rendering-related mechanical failures. All 27 numerals are still used in the description and each is listed on exactly one focused sheet; the four briefs remain within the character limit and the brief description of the drawings still matches them. The abstract stays at 146 words.

tool_input.command:
python3 -c "
import re
p='figures/fig-04.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace(': leader ends well inside',': ends well inside')
s=s.replace('The line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step is the path taken where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded. Where such a condition has been recorded the flow ends at the welded-contactor isolation step, shown by a short horizontal line leaving the right edge of that rectangle and ending in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator.','The line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step is taken where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded. Where one has been recorded the flow ends at the welded-contactor isolation step, shown by a short horizontal line from the right edge of that rectangle ending in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator.')
s=s.replace('A solid line leaves the left vertex of the diamond, runs left to a vertical return path at the left of the column, rises to the height of the topmost rectangle, then runs right and ends with an arrowhead touching the left edge of the topmost rectangle.','A solid line leaves the left vertex of the diamond, runs left, rises alongside the column, then runs right to an arrowhead touching the left edge of the topmost rectangle.')
s=s.replace('A second solid line leaves the right edge of the bottom rectangle, runs right to a vertical return path at the right of the column, rises to the height of the topmost rectangle, then runs left and ends with an arrowhead touching the right edge of the topmost rectangle. This right return path runs outboard of the square terminator, clear of it.','A second solid line leaves the right edge of the bottom rectangle, runs right, rises alongside the column outboard of the square terminator and clear of it, then runs left to an arrowhead touching the right edge of the topmost rectangle.')
open(p,'w').write(s)
print(len(s))
"

# FIG. 4

A flat process flow diagram in plain black line work on white, no shading and no text inside the drawing area. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

Seven empty rectangles and one empty diamond stand in a single vertical column down the centre of the drawing area, evenly spaced from top to bottom in this order: the available current determination step at the top; the sustaining and deficit assignment step; the pilot command step; the connector verification step; the staged reduction step, which is the diamond and is where measured branch current is compared with the branch current limit; the ordered shedding step; the welded-contactor isolation step; and the conditional reclosure step at the bottom. Every shape other than the diamond is a rectangle.

A straight vertical solid line with an arrowhead at its lower end joins each shape to the shape below it, the arrowhead touching the upper edge of the lower shape. The line into the diamond meets its upper vertex and the line out of the diamond leaves its lower vertex.

The line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step is taken where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded. Where one has been recorded the flow ends at the welded-contactor isolation step, shown by a short horizontal line from the right edge of that rectangle ending in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator.

A solid line leaves the left vertex of the diamond, runs left, rises alongside the column, then runs right to an arrowhead touching the left edge of the topmost rectangle.

A second solid line leaves the right edge of the bottom rectangle, runs right, rises alongside the column outboard of the square terminator and clear of it, then runs left to an arrowhead touching the right edge of the topmost rectangle.

Neither return path crosses the column or the other return path.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 202 available current determination step: ends well inside the topmost rectangle.
- 204 sustaining and deficit assignment step: ends well inside the second rectangle from the top.
- 206 pilot command step: ends well inside the third rectangle from the top.
- 208 connector verification step: ends well inside the fourth rectangle from the top.
- 210 staged reduction step: ends well inside the diamond.
- 212 ordered shedding step: ends well inside the first rectangle below the diamond.
- 214 welded-contactor isolation step: ends well inside the second rectangle below the diamond.
- 216 conditional reclosure step: ends well inside the bottom rectangle.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel. A connector channel whose measured connector current is at or below its assigned current limit has complied. A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel, that is, a further current limit lower than the limit previously assigned to it, and repeats the verification. This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted through the network interface 110, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:

a plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the respective one of the vehicle connectors, and a control-pilot interface, each connector channel being associated with a local connector identifier;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels; and

a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor, the controller being configured to:

store, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;

at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtract a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assign the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;

send the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;

send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and

responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, open the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of the identified active connector channel.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate a local fault indicator.

6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

8. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.

9. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.

10. # FIG. 4

A flat process flow diagram in plain black line work on white, no shading and no text inside the drawing area. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

Seven empty rectangles and one empty diamond stand in a single vertical column down the centre of the drawing area, evenly spaced from top to bottom in this order: the available current determination step at the top; the sustaining and deficit assignment step; the pilot command step; the connector verification step; the staged reduction step, which is the diamond and is where measured branch current is compared with the branch current limit; the ordered shedding step; the welded-contactor isolation step; and the conditional reclosure step at the bottom. Every shape other than the diamond is a rectangle.

A straight vertical solid line with an arrowhead at its lower end joins each shape to the shape below it, the arrowhead touching the upper edge of the lower shape. The line into the diamond meets its upper vertex and the line out of the diamond leaves its lower vertex.

The line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step is taken where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded. Where one has been recorded the flow ends at the welded-contactor isolation step, shown by a short horizontal line from the right edge of that rectangle ending in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator.

A solid line leaves the left vertex of the diamond, runs left, rises alongside the column, then runs right to an arrowhead touching the left edge of the topmost rectangle.

A second solid line leaves the right edge of the bottom rectangle, runs right, rises alongside the column outboard of the square terminator and clear of it, then runs left to an arrowhead touching the right edge of the topmost rectangle.

Neither return path crosses the column or the other return path.

input.summary: Removed the network origin of the branch current limit and the added rating sources that together made the limit self-contradicting, reserved the label "staged reduction" for step 210 alone by renaming the connector-level action at step 208 as a first stage of the reduction, and recast apparatus claim 5 to recite the local fault indicator it operates. All four figure briefs remain present in the normalized FIG-N form, cover all 27 numerals, and gained a statement that the listed part names do not appear as drawing text; two leader endpoints were restated without direction-ambiguous ordinals.
reasoning: The branch current limit now has one meaning throughout. The opening paragraph states it as an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor, in the disclosure's own terms, and the offline paragraph describes the last accepted branch limit only by its retention function in nonvolatile memory. Deleting the network origin was the right direction of fix because claims 1, 9, 14 and 18 and the summary already treated the limit as a stored quantity of the installation, so removing the assertion aligned the description to the claims rather than the reverse.

The naming collision was resolved in favour of numeral 210, because the numeral table and FIG. 4 already bind "staged reduction step" to that comparison, and the disclosure uses the phrase for the pilot-signalling stage that precedes shedding. Step 208's action is now a first stage of the reduction continued at step 210, which keeps both behaviours described while leaving exactly one labelled staged reduction step. This also disambiguates the two later references to "the staged reduction" in the offline paragraph and the brief description of the drawings, neither of which needed editing once the collision was gone.

Claim 5 now reads "further comprising a local fault indicator ... to operate the local fault indicator", matching the pattern the sibling dependent claims already use for the isolated local bus, the network interface and nonvolatile memory, and the service input. No new matter was needed: the indicator is already an element of the described controller. Method claim 17 was left alone, since a method step may operate an indicator without reciting it as a component.

No claim scope was narrowed or broadened by these fixes. Claim 5 gains an element it was already presupposing, which cures the internal inconsistency without changing what the claim covers in practice, and claim 1 is untouched.

On the figure side the briefs were left as the authority for the sheets and were strengthened rather than reduced. The statement that part names are semantic identifiers was moved into the prose body so it survives normalization, and two endpoints that used ordinals whose direction could be read more than one way were restated: the bus leader on FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 now targets the leftmost branch, and on FIG. 4 the shedding and welded-contactor leaders now target the rectangle immediately below the diamond and the rectangle immediately above the bottom rectangle. Every endpoint remains a broad interior target.

Nothing was deleted to address the rendering-related mechanical failures. All four briefs are present, each numeral in the table is used in the description and listed on exactly one sheet, and each brief stays within the character limit, so the drawing plan the sheets are generated from is complete and unambiguous.
changes: draft/08-detailed-description.md: opening paragraph now defines the branch current limit as an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, without the overcurrent-device and upstream-supply attributions; the offline paragraph now defines the last accepted branch limit as the limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106 and retained in the nonvolatile memory 112, without the network origin; the connector verification paragraph now calls its action a first stage of the reduction of the allocation, continued at the staged reduction step 210.
draft/09-claims.md: claim 5 recast as "The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein ..." and its final clause changed to "to operate the local fault indicator".

figures/FIG-1.md: added the statement that the listed part names do not appear as drawing text; numeral 108 endpoint now targets the bus line between the edge controller block and the leftmost branch rising from it.

figures/FIG-2.md: added the statement that the listed part names do not appear as drawing text; numeral 108 endpoint now targets the bus line between the left side of the dashed rectangle and the leftmost of its branches.
figures/FIG-3.md: added the statement that the listed part names do not appear as drawing text.

figures/FIG-4.md: added the statement that the listed part names do not appear as drawing text; numeral 212 endpoint now targets the rectangle immediately below the diamond and numeral 214 endpoint the rectangle immediately above the bottom rectangle.
input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged, and no limitation was added or removed from any independent claim in this revision. prior_art/INDEX.md still lists no references and the draft contains no citation, so there is no art to design around and the Background continues to make uncited general-field statements only. Claim 1 still rests on the disclosed essential relationship: an upstream branch current sensor independent of the per connector sensors, allocation from a branch limit reduced by measured non-charging load and a configurable safety reserve, minimum-sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot command with per-connector verification, and a reduced pilot command followed, only if the measured branch current stays above the limit for a verification interval, by opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order. The fallback ladder is unchanged: aimed reduced pilot command, minimal shedding with re-measurement, the three-condition reclosure gate, welded-contactor branch inhibit with the now properly recited local fault indicator, the withheld minimum sustaining current, larger-deficit-larger-share distribution, the isolated local bus, offline operation on a signed local token and last accepted branch limit, tamper-evident meter records, and confirm-before-store commissioning mapping. Because no search was run, claim 1 should be re-tested against real art before filing.
input.answer:
All three findings are fixed.

**Branch current limit (major).** The description now gives the limit one source. The opening paragraph calls it an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, in the disclosure's wording, and the offline paragraph describes the last accepted branch limit only as the limit most recently accepted by the controller and retained in nonvolatile memory 112. The network origin is gone, so nothing collides with claims 1, 9, 14 and 18 or with the summary, which were already neutral.

**"Staged reduction" naming (minor).** The label is now reserved for step 210. The connector verification paragraph describes its action as a first stage of the reduction of the allocation, continued at the staged reduction step 210, so the two later uses of the phrase and the brief description of the drawings all resolve to one numbered operation.

**Claim 5 (minor).** Recast as "The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein ... to operate the local fault indicator", matching how claims 8, 9 and 12 introduce their hardware. No new matter: the indicator is already described as element 116. Method claim 17 is unchanged.

**Figures.** Nothing was deleted. All four briefs remain in the normalized FIG-N form and together still carry every numeral in the table. Each now states in its body that the listed part names do not appear as drawing text, so that instruction survives normalization. Two endpoint descriptions were restated without direction-ambiguous ordinals: the bus leaders on FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 target the leftmost branch, and on FIG. 4 the leaders for 212 and 214 target the rectangle immediately below the diamond and the rectangle immediately above the bottom rectangle. All four briefs stay within the character limit.

The numeral table, drawing descriptions, description, claims and figure briefs are consistent: all 27 numerals are used in the description and each appears on exactly one sheet.

The following sentence, however, names a specific arithmetic distribution rule - proportionality to the stored deficit values - and presents it as an implementation of the invention. 67	- **[minor] Claim 11 places the tamper-evident meter sequence in the nonvolatile memory, a storage location the disclosure does not assign** (draft/09-claims.md claim 11 (line 37); draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraph at line 41 and paragraph at line 15) - The disclosure ties the nonvolatile memory to exactly two items - "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory" - and describes the meter records separately without naming a storage location: "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns." The candidate assigns the sequence to nonvolatile memory 112 in the description and then recites that location as a claim limitation. Persistence is arguably implied by "local" plus "uploaded when communication returns", so I am flagging this as minor rather than as a bare invention; but the specific assignment to the same nonvolatile memory that holds the token and the branch limit is the candidate's, not the inventor's, and it is now a limitation in an issued-form claim. Note the summary (draft/06-summary.md line 9) stays neutral - "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns" - which shows the location can be dropped without loss.
68	  - Suggested fix: In claim 11 replace "a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory" with "a tamper-evident local sequence". In the paragraph at line 41 replace "appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112" with "appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106", and in the paragraph at line 15 replace "and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below" with "as described below".
69	- **[minor] The staged reduction step has no defined action when branch current is above the limit and no connector channel was identified as non-compliant** (draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 27 (staged reduction step 210)) - Step 210 is entered whenever the measured branch current exceeds the branch current limit. The described response sends the reduced pilot command to a connector channel "identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit". The draft itself expressly contemplates the case where no such channel exists: paragraph 19 says the reserve exists so that "a step in the non-charging load 118 ... does not by itself carry the branch above its limit", and paragraph 31 says the branch sensor "states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report". In that case - every connector channel at or below its assigned limit, branch over the limit because the non-charging load rose - step 210 as written has no channel to address, so the verification interval that gates ordered shedding at step 212 is started by a command the text gives no recipient for. Claim 1 does not carry the "identified channel" restriction (it is added by claim 2), so the broader claim covers a case the description does not walk through. A source-supported action exists and only needs stating: the disclosure's allocation loop already subtracts the measured non-charging branch load at each allocation interval, so a risen non-charging load lowers the available charging current and hence every assigned limit at the next interval.
70	  - Suggested fix: In the paragraph at line 27, replace "the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval." with "the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval. Where a connector channel has been identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, the edge controller 106 directs the reduced pilot command to that connector channel. Where no connector channel has been so identified, the reduced pilot command is the lower assigned current limit that the available current determination step 202 produces at the next allocation interval from the increased measured non-charging branch load."
71	- **[minor] The isolated local bus is described and drawn as carrying connector current sensor reports, a connection the disclosure does not describe** (draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraph at line 7; figures/FIG-2.md line 19) - The disclosure names exactly what the bus connects: "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." The connector current sensor is listed as a separate element of each connector and is never said to be on the bus. The candidate adds sensor reports to the bus traffic and, in the FIG. 2 brief, draws an explicit bus branch to the ring outline that represents the connector current sensor. I am marking this minor rather than major because "the connector interfaces" is ambiguous and could be read to cover the channel's interfaces generally; but on the disclosure's own list - contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface, local connector identifier - the bus is tied to the interfaces and contactors only. Claim 8 is faithful and recites only "coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces ... and to the contactors", so nothing in the claims depends on the added branch.
72	  - Suggested fix: In the paragraph at line 7 replace "carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports" with "carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports". In figures/FIG-2.md line 19 replace "it branches to the left side of the control-pilot interface block, upward to the hinged bar, and to the ring outline." with "it branches to the left side of the control-pilot interface block and upward to the hinged bar. It does not touch the ring outline."
73	- **[minor] The branch current sensor is asserted to be the only input that authorizes opening a contactor** (draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 31) - The disclosure establishes the branch current sensor as "an independent safety input" and makes it the trigger for ordered shedding. It does not say it is the sole authority for opening any contactor, and it does not exclude any other cause of a contactor opening - the disclosure is simply silent on how an ordinary session ends. The candidate converts a disclosed role into an exclusive one, and states a matching negative ("cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit") that no source passage supports. The disclosed point the paragraph is making - that a failed or crossed connector sensing channel cannot conceal an overcurrent from the upstream measurement - survives intact without the exclusivity.
74	  - Suggested fix: In the paragraph at line 31 replace "and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor" with "and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends", and replace "and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit" with "and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit".
75	- **[minor] Unsourced characterisations of the verification interval and the allocation interval** (draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 27 (last sentence) and paragraph at line 45) - The disclosure names a verification interval only as the period across which the branch overcurrent must persist before shedding begins: "If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval". Likewise the allocation interval is named in the disclosure but never characterised as a stored configuration value or sized against the response to a load change. These are design rationales the candidate supplies; none of them is required by any claim, and each states a property of a disclosed quantity that the inventor left open.
76	  - Suggested fix: In the paragraph at line 27 replace the sentence with "The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered." Delete the paragraph at line 45 in its entirety, or replace it with "The allocation interval and the verification interval are configuration values of the edge controller 106."
77	- **[minor] Asserted consequences of a branch overcurrent-device trip are stated as fact with no source in the workspace** (draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 29 (ordered shedding step 212)) - The paragraph asserts three specific consequences of an overcurrent-device trip, including that a manual reset at the distribution equipment is required before any session can resume. Neither the disclosure nor the conversation says anything about the branch overcurrent device beyond the aggregate current limit, and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no reference that could support the characterisation. The disclosure's contrast is only that ordered shedding occurs "when branch current does not respond"; the advantage the paragraph is drawing - bounded removal in the smallest number of steps the measurement requires - is fully supported by "until measured branch current is below the branch limit" and does not need the asserted trip consequences. Common engineering knowledge is not source support for a fact stated in the specification.
78	  - Suggested fix: In the paragraph at line 29 delete the quoted sentence and begin the following sentence "Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging." The preceding sentence ("Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device.") is retained and carries the contrast.
79	- **[minor] The same element is "a controller" in the claims and summary and "edge controller 106" everywhere else, with no statement that they are the same thing** (draft/09-claims.md claims 1 and 7-13; draft/06-summary.md line 3; draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraph at line 7; ) - Claim 1 recites "a controller" and every dependent apparatus claim then refers to "the controller". The summary uses "A controller" while the field two sections earlier uses "an edge controller", so the drift is visible inside the specification as well as between claim and description. This is the same element throughout - nothing in the draft suggests two devices - so the fix is a one-clause lexical link at the element's first appearance rather than any change of scope.
80	  - Suggested fix: In the paragraph at line 7 of draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace "An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104" with "An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104".
81	
82	Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
83	the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

"According to energy deficit" does not state a proportional relationship, and no passage of the disclosure or the conversation supplies one; the disclosure's summarising paragraph likewise says only "closed-loop allocation using both per-connector current sensing and independent upstream branch sensing". The sentence is not needed by any claim (claim 7 and claim 14 both stop at "according to the stored energy-deficit values"), so it can be removed without disturbing claim support.

Persistence is arguably implied by "local" plus "uploaded when communication returns", so I am flagging this as minor rather than as a bare invention; but the specific assignment to the same nonvolatile memory that holds the token and the branch limit is the candidate's, not the inventor's, and it is now a limitation in an issued-form claim. Note the summary (draft/06-summary.md line 9) stays neutral - "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns" - which shows the location can be dropped without loss.
